From: Olivia Parker <olivia.parker@hexaretail.com>

Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency on streaming chat during peak — urgent

Hi Dev,

We hit a big regression this morning on our live chat during the 09:00 ET marketing blast. p95 is fine but p99 for streaming responses (WebSocket) spiked to ~2.1s and a few clients saw dropouts. This only impacts the streaming endpoint — non-streaming completions were normal. We've attached a short client-side trace and a screenshot of the spike.

What we see: many short-lived frames, partial chunks, then a long tail. Turned on verbose logs and captured a few request ids. Can you confirm if anything changed on your side (routing, autoscale, or model variants)? This is causing customer complaints and impacting our support SLAs.

Attached: screenshot_latency_chart.png, client_trace_0815.txt

Regards,
Olivia Parker
Head of Integrations — HexaRetail
From: dev_patel@redwood.ai

Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency on streaming chat during peak — urgent

Hi Olivia — thanks for the data, we're on it. Quick triage notes:
- Routing and model catalog had no pushes in the last 24h.
- We are seeing elevated queue depth for the streaming workers in the us-east region coincident with your spike window.
- Request IDs look like they routed through the standard streaming pool (stream-v2).

I'm escalating to SRE (Rishi) and ops to check autoscaling and any transient IO/backpressure. Can you share one full request id that shows chunk delay? We'll pull worker logs and KV cache traces.

Next steps (internal): Rishi to validate worker queue/backpressure, Sean to check edge/network telemetry.

--
Dev Patel

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Unexpected latency on streaming chat during peak — urgent

Quick hit from infra: we see bursty CPU saturation on streaming shard group s-12 between 09:03-09:12 ET and elevated epoll wait times on the worker process. IO to kv-cache also shows occasional multi-second stall events correlated with the same request window. Hypothesis: under peak fanout, our backpressure algorithm is thrashing and causing head-of-line blocking for a subset of streams.

Immediate mitigations I pushed:
- Raised streaming worker concurrency limit by 20% for us-east (temporary).
- Forced a fallback to the non-chunking streaming mode for connections from HexaRetail (config toggle).

I also kicked a scale-up for additional stream workers. Monitoring now.

Attaching: hexaretail-spike-logs.zip (trimmed logs, worker traces)

Rishi
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Live feeds backpressure — HexaRetail streaming p99 surge

Hi Olivia — quick summary and next steps: 

What happened (short): during HexaRetail's 09:00 ET peak on 2027-08-15, a subset of streaming worker processes experienced transient backpressure when concurrent connection fanout spiked. This produced a p99 latency regression (~2.1s) on the streaming/WebSocket endpoint for a small fraction (~0.6%) of sessions. Non-streaming requests were unaffected.

What we did (immediate):
- Raised stream worker concurrency and scaled additional workers in us-east.
- Temporarily toggled non-chunked streaming for your connections to reduce head-of-line blocking.
- Stabilized KV-cache IO paths to reduce stall windows.

Current status: metrics returned close to baseline after the mitigations; we're continuing to monitor through your next scheduled campaigns.

Proposed remediation offer:
- 5% service credit for the impacted billing period (we're happy to make this 10% if you prefer a faster dedicated routing trial).
- If you expect recurring high-fanout blasts, we can onboard you to a dedicated streaming pool for the campaign window (trial 2 weeks, fee-waived for onboarding).

Next steps:
- (Action) HexaRetail to share any additional request IDs showing residual trouble.
- (Action) Redwood to run a focused load test simulating your campaign profile and provide a postmortem by Tue 2027-08-17 EOD.

Attachments: hexaretail-spike-logs.zip, screenshot_latency_chart.png

Would you like a quick sync today to walk through mitigations?

Thanks for raising this — sorry for the disruption. We'll get this locked down.

Best,
Dev Patel
